chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Shu'ayb al-Aqarqufi, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who dies and has no household goods left. He said, 'The sword.' And he said, 'When the dead man dies, his son has the sword, the saddle (for riding), and the clothes (as) the clothes of his skin.'

key_terms.ثِيَابَ جِلْدِهِ: the clothes of his skin (idiom for worn clothing)

ai.seo_question: What does a son inherit from his father if there are no other household goods left?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that in the absence of other movable property, a son inherits the father's sword, saddle, and worn clothing, which is metaphorically described as 'the clothes of his skin' to emphasize its intimate association with the deceased. This ruling highlights the practical prioritization of essential personal effects in early Shia inheritance jurisprudence, reflecting the material conditions of the time where such items held significant economic and functional value.
